messages:
maya: Quick sanity check — we got a spike of partial WS frames + a bunch of 1006 closes on blue/region-e this morning around 09:12. Anyone know the fastest place to grab end-to-end traces + the raw nginx/envoy logs for a session id? Trying to correlate chunk timing with socket closes.

santiago: @maya the good starting points are the streaming dashboard (ops -> streaming -> ws-overview) and the trace link in the request table. For raw logs check: https://dash.redwood/streams/logs?service=ingress&env=region-e

eli: Also grep the ingress for the connection id header we inject: `X-Conn-Id`. e.g.

journalctl -u ingress --no-pager | grep X-Conn-Id | grep "<conn-id>"

That will show upstream disconnect reasons in the same timeline.

maya: thanks — is there a trace/span name I should filter for to see chunk timing? the per-token metrics look fine but chunks arrive delayed then socket drops.

santiago: filter spans named `ws.stream.frame` and `ws.stream.kvcache`. There's a tag `frame.size` and `frame.delay_ms`. Query in tracing: `service:ingress and span:ws.stream.frame and tags.frame.delay_ms>50`

eli: FYI we saw a TLS reneg handshake on one host earlier that caused full TCP teardown -> 1006. check envoy log lines with `transport_socket` and `close_code=1006`.

maya: good point — how do I map a trace id to the host that handled the ws? the trace shows ingress but not host by default.

santiago: trace has `host` attr but our UI hides it in condensed view. Expand span metadata or use this trace query param: `&showFields=host,conn_meta`. Also the trace link in dashboard has an `expand` toggle.

runtime-oncall: deploy-bot says a small ingress cert rotation happened @ 09:05 on region-e, rollout completed by 09:08. If your spikes are 09:12 might be related to tail hosts still reconnecting :warning:

deploy-bot: deploy: ingress-cert-rotation completed for region-e in 6m — changed cert chain on nodes 12-18. No errors reported in rollout job.

eli: If you suspect cert rotation, add a quick alert to watch partial-frame ratio per-host: `alert if partial_frames / total_frames > 0.02 for 5m` and scope to region-e. For now keep it as warning-only to avoid noise.

maya: created an ad-hoc trace with conn-id from a failed session and see repeated `ws.stream.frame` delays ~120ms leading to a `connection_reset` on the next read. Host shows node-14 which was in the rotated set.

santiago: sounds like a plausible root. Two action items: (1) revert node-14 from rotation pool and repro, (2) add correlation-id logging to ingress `onFrame` path so future traces show frame index. I can send a small PR for (2) — @eli can you review?

eli: yep, ping me the PR. For (1) we can cordon node-14 in k8s and watch traffic move off it, then re-run the client repro.

maya: pinged with the PR link. I'll cordon node-14 now and re-run the client repro in 5.

santiago: also adding a tweak to the alert: temporarily raise partial-frame threshold to 3% for region-e while we validate, then drop back.

maya: re-run done — repro looks quieter after cordon. I still see a handful of 1006 but much fewer. Collecting a final trace and sending to #incidents if we want a postmortem.

eli: nice. After PR lands let's add a tiny metric (`frame.index` in spans) — will make debugging easier.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll post follow-up with final traces and the cordon timeline. :white_check_mark:
